correctness.rationale: For the specified relation-free three-vertex path algebra, fixing the vertices forces the arrow images into their endpoint corners. The maps on the two consecutive arrow spaces are S and T, the map on direct arrows is (D,B), and the map on length-two paths is P=S⊗T. There are no unstated multiplicativity conditions. Idempotence requires S,T,D to be projections and BD+PB=B. Splitting by image and kernel gives exactly B(im D)⊆ker P and B(ker D)⊆im P, in every characteristic. This gives the stated power of q, independently of the Gaussian-binomial counts of image/kernel decompositions. The corner image projects onto im D and meets the path space in im P, so its rank is d+ab. All triples occur, and lowering a or b from the maximal pair costs at least two ranks, proving the codimension-one coefficient and both unique extremes. The small example was recomputed from I_2(2,k)=(1,6,1): the coefficients in ascending attainable-rank order are (1,28,194,104,288,48,48,16,1), totaling 728; neither 7 nor 8 occurs as a product (a+1)(b+1), hence rank 10 cannot occur for t=1. This finite arithmetic supplements the general proof, not the converse.
residual_risks: The counting argument does not cover moving vertex idempotents, relations in the path algebra, or longer quivers.

value.rationale: The smallest acyclic bypass geometry in which direct-arrow and path images share a corner gives a natural test of split algebra images. The formula counts labeled splitting maps including the path-valued shear multiplicities, and gives a field-independent forbidden codimension-two rank in the exhibited example despite the adjacent ranks occurring. This supplies useful exact data not recoverable from counting linear projections alone.
residual_risks: Scope is the specified anchored family, not a classification of unanchored retractions or all quiver rank spectra.
